sections.h2: Where does Franklin County, TN keep its deed records?
sections.html:
Deeds are filed at 1 South Jefferson Street in Winchester, TN 37398, the county seat, and the register's line is (931) 967-2840. Nancy K. Ringer is listed as Register, and the office shares a courthouse address with the assessor and the trustee.

The register's website describes the job broadly. The office creates and preserves a record of each instrument the law requires or allows to be filed, among them deeds, mortgages, liens and plats, along with leases, wills, court orders and military discharges. Those records give public notice of who owns land and what claims sit against it, and the papers stay in the county seat.

For a house sale, the deed that moves title to your buyer is indexed in Winchester, and so is the paper that releases your old loan.

sections.h2: Which Franklin County offices does a seller deal with?
sections.html:
Three offices share the courthouse at 1 South Jefferson Street, so most of a seller's errands can be done in one trip. The register records, the assessor values, and the trustee collects the tax.

Franklin County offices at the Winchester courthouse
OfficeRole in a salePhone
Register of DeedsRecords the deed and releases(931) 967-2840
Property Assessor (Room 101)Appraises and assesses each parcel(931) 967-3869
Trustee (P.O. Box 340)Collects property tax(931) 967-2962

Source: Franklin County Property Assessor, Franklin County Trustee and the Register of Deeds site. The assessor's counter runs weekdays from eight until half past four.

The assessor's office keeps an individual property record card on every parcel in the county, about 25,000 in all. Records are updated weekly through the state's Local Assessor System for web viewing, and a public terminal at the office can pull them up. Before you set an asking price, have the staff read back the owner of record and the property classification.

sections.h2: What transfer tax would a Winchester-area sale carry?
sections.html:
On a transfer of real property the state takes 37 cents for each $100 of the price or value, and the buyer pays it to the register at recording. The 2020-2024 Census estimate puts a typical owned home here at $236,900, which would owe about $876.53.

A mortgage tax of 11.5 cents per $100 of debt applies to new loans after the first $2,000, and the borrower covers it.

Whichever is higher, the price paid or the property's value, sets the tax base, and the buyer swears to it before the register. A deed that cites a statutory exemption skips the oath. The exempt list includes ending a tenancy by the entirety and releasing a life estate to the beneficiaries.

sections.h2: Why might the Franklin County register refuse a deed?
sections.html:
The register checks whether a paper can be accepted and leaves its legal effect to the drafter. The University of Tennessee's county advisory staff lists what a deed needs.

  • Readable text and a notary's acknowledgment (Tennessee Code sections 66-24-101 and 66-22-101)
  • Names and addresses of the owner and the taxpayer, section 66-24-114
  • A derivation clause that cites the prior deed, section 66-24-110
  • The drafter's name and address, section 66-24-115
  • The parcel number, section 66-24-122
  • Fees, plus transfer tax if any is owed, on the day of filing

A document in another language needs a translation attached, and registers may turn away an unreadable page. One missing item sends the deed back, which can push a closing date. Compare the parcel number on the deed with the one on your tax bill before anyone signs.

sections.h2: What is Franklin County like for a home seller?
sections.html:
Franklin County lies on the Alabama line at the eastern boundary of Middle Tennessee. It covers 576 square miles, of which 555 are land, and it climbs from the Nashville Basin over the Highland Rim and onto the Cumberland Plateau, a rise of about 1,300 feet. The county was organized in 1807 and named for Benjamin Franklin, and Winchester is the seat.

The county's own website lists the University of the South at Sewanee, Tims Ford Reservoir and State Park, and a manufacturing base tied to the automotive industry. Wikipedia adds that Nissan built a large engine plant at Decherd and that the Arnold Engineering Development Center lies partly in the county. Cowan, Decherd, Estill Springs, Sewanee, Huntland, Sherwood and Winchester are the communities named on the county site, and Interstate 24 gives access to Chattanooga.

Settlement by white families began around 1800, and in the twentieth century the Tennessee Valley Authority brought flood control, power and new lakes. The same projects displaced residents whose homes were flooded. Wikipedia notes that in the 2020 census the county had 19,395 housing units, 13.3 percent of them vacant, and that about two thirds of residents lived in rural areas.

The Census Bureau's QuickFacts put numbers on the housing picture:

  • 45,579 residents in the July 2025 estimate, up 6.6 percent from the 2020 base
  • 77.4 percent owner-occupied, with a median gross rent of $894
  • Median household income of $63,494 and a median home value of $236,900
  • 22.5 percent of residents are 65 or older
  • 323 building permits issued in 2025

Median household income here is below the $75,003 of neighboring Dickson County and the $88,456 of Fayette County in the same Census table.

sections.h2: What do Franklin County owners need to know about the tax calendar?
sections.html:
Under the Comptroller's schedule the assessment date is January 1. Bills fall due the first Monday in October, and February 28 is the final day to pay with no interest. Balances are delinquent from March 1.

State law makes the assessor responsible for locating and identifying every taxable property in Franklin County, appraising it and setting its assessed value. The trustee bills and collects but has no say over the appraisal, so a complaint about value goes to the assessor first. The assessor says the commission sets the rate.

The Comptroller's tax calculator says a home is assessed at a quarter of its appraised value. For a $236,900 house that is $59,225, and the tax is that figure divided by 100 and multiplied by the rate. Ask the trustee for the current rate and balance.

Challenges go first to the board of equalization for the county, which convenes June 1. Elderly or disabled owners with 2025 income of $38,470 or less may qualify for state relief, and the form goes to the trustee within 35 days after the delinquency date.

faqs.q: Where do I record a deed in Franklin County, Tennessee?
faqs.a: At the Register of Deeds, 1 South Jefferson Street in Winchester, TN 37398. Call (931) 967-2840. The register is Nancy K. Ringer, and the office is in the county seat.

faqs.q: Who do I call to check my Franklin County property tax?
faqs.a: Call the Franklin County Trustee at (931) 967-2962. The trustee collects the tax, while the Property Assessor at (931) 967-3869 handles the appraisal and assessment.

faqs.q: How many parcels does the Franklin County assessor track?
faqs.a: About 25,000. The assessor keeps a property record card on each parcel, updated weekly through the state's Local Assessor System for web viewing.

faqs.q: How much is transfer tax on a Franklin County house worth $236,900?
faqs.a: About $876.53. Tennessee charges $0.37 per $100 of the price or value, and the buyer pays it when the deed is recorded.

faqs.q: Which communities are in Franklin County, Tennessee?
faqs.a: The county website names Cowan, Decherd, Estill Springs, Sewanee, Huntland, Sherwood and Winchester, with Winchester as the county seat. Sewanee is home to the University of the South.
